title: Rain garden and allotment drainage

threads.title: Library rain garden
threads.scope: Design, install and assess a rain garden beside the Birch Lane library to intercept roof runoff.

threads.title: Allotment plot drainage
threads.scope: Improve drainage in allotment plot 18 so its vegetable beds stop waterlogging.

threads.title: Cello audition recording
threads.scope: Prepare and record two cello pieces for a conservatory audition submission.

captures.text: Birch Lane library wants a rain garden to catch roof runoff. Survey the downpipe, size the basin, then check it after the first storm.
captures.rationale: Design through post-storm assessment form one named installation.

captures.text: Photo description: allotment plot 18 vegetable beds under standing water. Separate drainage job: cut a shallow side swale without routing water into neighboring plots.
captures.rationale: A distinct site and practical goal establish another drainage project.

captures.text: Library downpipe survey: the runoff crosses the paving first. The rain-garden inlet needs a stone apron so the basin edge will not wash out.
captures.rationale: Site survey and inlet design continue the library project.

captures.text: Cello audition checklist: record the prelude and the dance in one quiet room, then choose complete takes for the submission.
captures.rationale: A music audition has no supported connection to the drainage work.

captures.text: Skip the membrane; roots need to cross.
captures.rationale: Both landscape jobs involve soil and roots; the fragment gives no site.

captures.text: Library rain-garden planting plan: sedges near the inlet, flowering plugs on the higher rim. Basin depth shown as 250 mm.
captures.rationale: Planting layout is part of the runoff installation.

captures.text: The membrane note refers to plot 18's vegetable-bed swale. Leave it unlined so crop roots can cross; the library basin uses its own specification.
captures.rationale: Names the specific site behind the earlier fragment.

captures.text: Order from Flint Yard: washed stone for Birch Lane library rain-garden inlet; separate gravel bags for plot 18's swale. Invoice lines have separate site codes.
captures.rationale: A common supplier document directly serves both distinct jobs.

captures.text: Installation clip at Birch Lane library: inlet stone apron is seated, basin is excavated to the revised depth, and the sedges are planted.
captures.rationale: Executes the revised design of the library rain garden.

captures.text: Plot 18 after rain: the new unlined side swale drains, but a low corner of the vegetable bed still holds water. Raise only that corner.
captures.rationale: Assessment and targeted revision continue the allotment project.

captures.text: Library rain garden after its first storm: water entered over the stone apron, no rim erosion, standing water gone by the following morning.
captures.rationale: The planned storm assessment evaluates the same installed basin.

captures.text: Library rain-garden handover: keep the inlet free of leaves and recheck the sedges in six weeks. Attach the first-storm observations to the maintenance sheet.
captures.rationale: Handover and initial maintenance remain part of the installation project.

events.text: Library rain-garden planting plan revised: sedges near the inlet, flowering plugs on the higher rim. Basin depth is 200 mm after checking the buried service clearance.

events.reason: c07 explicitly places the membrane instruction at allotment plot 18. Assign it to that drainage job.

challenges: Similar drainage methods do not collapse separate sites.
A changed dimension preserves project identity.
An invoice can span projects while its lines remain separately allocated.
Maintenance and evaluation can continue an installation project.
authorNotes: All sites and observations are fictional. No horticultural or engineering recommendation is being made for a real location.
